title.narrative: Institutional strengthening of national level bodies for technical and vocational education in Ghana in terms of accreditation, supervision and management and by making ATVET Competence Based

description.narrative:
**Impact**
The proposed project will contribute to End hunger (SDG 2) and manifest in the following long term impacts:
- Reduce Malnutrition - Promote agricultural growth - Ecologically sustainable food systems
**Objective**
Contribute To end hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture (SDG 2) through the strengthening of capacity, knowledge and quality of individuals as well as organisations in the fields of Technical and Vocational Education and Training and Higher Education (TVET/HE) in OKP partner countries.
- Number of people lifted out of undernourishment is increased by 5% - Number of family farms (sub-sector, male/female, age) that doubled their productivity and/or income is increased by 10-15% - Number of hectares of farmland converted to sustainable use is increased by 5-10%

- Management and staff of MOFA - Management and staff of regulatory national bodies (COTVET, TEU and NABPTEX) - Management, teaching staff of Kwadaso (medium-term because Kwadaso is pilot college) and - all Farming Institutes and Agricultural colleges in the long-term.

comment.narrative:
06-09-2023: A total of 22 courses have been developed during the complete project implementation phase, for year 4 14 courses have been finalized.
6 – new curriculum that were started at the beginning of the project are all completed in year 4 and approved. 14-short courses have been developed out of the 6 approved curricula and are ready for implementation. 2 CSA short courses were developed. Making it 22 in total.

10-12-2020: The curricula development process has been initiated. In June 2020, occupational standards have been developed and validated by all relevant stakeholders managed by COTVET. COTVET has just announced the approval of the Occupational standards of the following educational programs for further processes of the curriculum development to proceed: - Livestock and Meat Production, - Agribusiness, - Mechanization and Irrigation, - Tree Crop Production, - Arable Crop, - Poultry Value Chain.

29-01-2022: At the moment 6 curriculum courses are being developed according to the procedures of CTVET. These will be incorporated into the NQF. After accreditation of these courses, some of the content will be used to convert them in 4 extra short courses or more per each accredited curriculum which can be used in the Farm Institutes. Due to the COVID 19 pandemic this process got a delay and will now be completed in year 3.

title.narrative: A.E.3. Number of staff that have gained qualitative and relevant knowledge and skills to develop and offer the revised/developed study programmes

comment.narrative:
06-09-2023: 57 individuals benefitted from additional training during the final project year. These individuals have participated in trainings in previous years. The trainings provided are the following:
12 staff from the 3-Farm Institutes (FI) and CTVET participated in branding, publicity and enrolment trainings to build their capacities to reach target groups for enrolment into the developed programs.
12 staff from FI were involved in CSA-insects production ToT as part of the preparations towards the implementation of the new curricula as well as for boosting sustainable efficient poultry and fish production through alternative protein sources with reduced cost.
12 staff from the FIs and CTVET had participated in a short course development training and produced 12 short courses out of the 6-developed curricula.
12 staff from CTVET, MOE and MOFA participated in a study visit to the Netherlands to learn best practices for adaption and adoption to aid the efficient implementation of the new curricula developed.
9 staff from the FI embaked on a regional study visit to Benin Songhai center to learn from their experiences for possible adaption and adoption of their best practices.
Of the 57 whom participated in training in year 4 the division between male and females is:
Male: 38 Female: 19
Of the 57 whom participated in training in year 4 the division between teachers and admin is:
A total of 39 staff are teachers from the FIs. The 18 are admins from CTVET, MOE and MOFA.
All the trainings and capacity building activities have been in the short-term mode. The project did not plan for other modes of training (MSC or PHD).

06-09-2023: In total we trained at least 48 unique participants in Y3. Some of these individuals were reached with multiple training offerings:
30 staff from the FI were trained in CBET teaching methodologies and were registered by CTVET to qualify them to implement the newly developed CBET curriculum for Poultry, Agripreneurship etc.
10 staff from CTVET communication and corporate affairs unit also received training in communication and marketing and to develop communication and marketing strategies for purposes of implementing strategies to market CTVET and its allied Institutions.
Also, 15 FI staff were also involved in the strategic planning workshops as ToTs to guide the others in their respective Institutues in the development of strategic plans for the Institutes.
Again, 15 FI staff were also involved in the development of Learning Materials, Assessment, re-assessment and marking guidelines for the new curriculum that were submitted to CTVET for assessment.
Additionally, 10 staff from CTVET, 6 from the FI and 8 from the Children’s homes (minority groups) from the Department of Social Welfare in Ghana were also involved in training workshops on developing strategies for inclusion of minorities and marginalized groups in ATVET landscape.

10-12-2020: A TNA has been executed among the 3 National bodies providing insight in the existing knowledge & skills. During the development of the Occupational Standards, practical knowledge & skills have been used and adapted when needed.
29-01-2022: 23 Staff members of CTVET trained by the project

21-02-2023: CTVET supported the identification of relevant Agro companies within the catchment areas of the FIs for purposes of workplace experience learning (WEL). It also facilitated the signing of the MOUs with the FIs by making available its developed WEL format and guidelines for the MOU development.

29-01-2022: Preparations have been going on, companies have been identified and initial discussions to lead to MOU signing have started despite the travel restrictions. The project aims to get the agreements signed and the assignment finalized in year 3, despite the delays due to COVID 19

comment.narrative: 06-09-2023: This is achieved in year 3 although a new batch of graduates will be churned out later in September

10-12-2020: The strategic plans of the National Bodies will be assessed, and support still needs to be organized for their implementation. Instrumental for achieving this is the current ongoing curriculum development process and outcome of the OKP-GHA-103458 project.

21-02-2023: Currently, the two new approved curricula for the FIs (Poultry and Agripreneuship NCII) have 115 students following the course. Curricula and teachers have just been accredited. The project now works on getting the farm institutes accredited. But even before the formal accreditation of the Institutues for the formal implementation to start, the FI have replaced the old FI curriculum and have started using the new one.
